_format: skill-creator eval format. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions. expect_trigger false marks a should-not-trigger probe.

evals.prompt: Our CLAUDE.md is 500 lines and AGENTS.md is a slightly different copy of it. Claude keeps ignoring half of it. Clean this up properly.
assertions: Measures before editing (runs scripts/measure.py or reports line/byte counts and the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md relation)
Produces an inventory that assigns each section a destination: keep, docs/, hook or CI, skill, path rule, or delete
Makes AGENTS.md the canonical file and reduces CLAUDE.md to an @AGENTS.md import on its first line instead of a symlink or second copy
Moves knowledge into docs/ with a pointer row rather than deleting it outright
Proposes turning at least one must-always-hold rule into a hook, linter or CI check instead of prose

evals.prompt: Every time someone runs composer install, php artisan boost:install rewrites AGENTS.md and our hand-written project rules disappear. How do we stop losing them?
assertions: Explains that everything inside the laravel-boost-guidelines block is regenerated and hand-written text there is lost
Moves standing instructions to .ai/guidelines and project knowledge to docs/
Mentions the .gitignore pattern .ai/* with !.ai/guidelines/ when .ai is ignored
Proposes a CI check that regenerates and fails on any diff, using the same flags as the automatic run

evals.prompt: I put my own company's conventions in ~/.claude/rules, but now they show up when I work in a client's repo and contradict their rules. How should I set this up?
assertions: States that ~/.claude/rules and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md load in every project and that conflicting levels are resolved arbitrarily
Recommends scoping the company rules by an ancestor-directory CLAUDE.md (or a plugin/managed route for a team) instead of user-level rules
Suggests verifying in a fresh session in both a company repo and a client repo

evals.prompt: Set up the agent instructions for this repo. The team uses Claude Code, Cursor and opencode, and we want to try OpenHands.
assertions: Creates AGENTS.md as the canonical file and CLAUDE.md containing @AGENTS.md
Leads with commands the agent cannot guess (install, test, lint with flags) rather than an architecture overview
Places skills in .agents/skills with .claude/skills as a symlink to it
Keeps AGENTS.md well under 32 KiB and under roughly 200 lines

evals.prompt: CLAUDE.md says never edit files in public/build, but Claude keeps running sed on them anyway. How do I make that stick?
assertions: Recommends enforcement instead of rewording the rule: a permission deny rule and a PreToolUse hook
Points out that an Edit(...) deny rule does not cover Bash writes such as sed -i
Uses exit code 2 (not 1) for the blocking hook
Suggests testing the hook by piping a sample event into it

evals.prompt: A contractor opened a PR that changes AGENTS.md, adds a .mcp.json and edits .claude/settings.json. What should I check before merging?
assertions: Runs or recommends measure.py --security-only (or an equivalent scan for hidden Unicode characters)
Flags enableAllProjectMcpServers, unpinned npx MCP packages, broad permission grants and hooks or env such as *_BASE_URL as review points
Treats hooks and env in settings as code changes that need the same review as code

evals.prompt: I rewrote a rule in our AGENTS.md. How do I prove the new wording actually changes what the agent does?
assertions: Proposes probe tasks run in fresh sessions with and without the change, e.g. scripts/probe.py
Recommends about 10 runs per arm and says 3 runs prove nothing
Grades deterministically (tool-call regex or a command run afterwards) before any LLM judge

evals.prompt: Write a README for this repository that explains to new developers what the project does and how to run it.
assertions: Writes a README without treating it as an agent instruction file

evals.prompt: Write a new Claude skill that formats our changelog entries.
assertions: Treats the task as skill authoring, not as editing CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md

evals.prompt: After upgrading Laravel Boost, our CLAUDE.md that only contained @AGENTS.md suddenly has the whole <laravel-boost-guidelines> block in it again. What happened and how do we stop it?
assertions: Explains that newer Boost writes its guideline block into an existing CLAUDE.md unless the Claude Code guidelines_path is configured
Fixes it by setting config('boost.agents.claude_code.guidelines_path') to AGENTS.md in config/boost.php
Restores CLAUDE.md to a hand-written file whose first line is @AGENTS.md instead of deleting CLAUDE.md or symlinking it
Adds or keeps a CI check that fails when CLAUDE.md contains a generated block

evals.prompt: We added our company package's Boost guideline to guidelines.exclude in config/boost.php, but after boost:install its text still shows up in AGENTS.md. We had overridden it in .ai/guidelines before. Why?
assertions: Identifies that the leftover .ai/guidelines override of the package guideline is promoted to a standalone guideline when the package guideline is excluded
Tells the user to delete the override file under .ai/guidelines together with the exclude
Uses the exact guideline key form vendor/package/path in the exclude list
Regenerates and confirms the text is gone, rather than editing AGENTS.md by hand

evals.prompt: In our Laravel Boost repo I want rules that only load when an agent works on migrations or tests, and Claude Code should pick them up by itself without that 'you MUST first open .ai/rules/index.md' paragraph. Set it up.
assertions: Puts the rules in .ai/rules/*.md with paths: frontmatter, flat, and re-includes .ai/rules/ in .gitignore
Creates a committed .claude/rules symlink pointing to ../.ai/rules so Claude Code loads matching rules natively
Sets rules.enabled to false in config/boost.php so the always-on index paragraph disappears
Keeps each rule short (what to do, why, link to the docs section) instead of moving the full explanation into the rule
Adds a CI check that every rule glob matches at least one file and that its links resolve
